title: How do we add a truly custom provider (like NASA's M20 Mars feed)?
description:
NASA is maintaining an excellent tiles API for the Jezero Crater area, "home" to the Perseverance Rover and the Ingenuity helicopter drone:

https://mars.nasa.gov/mmgis-maps/M20/Layers/M20_HiRISE_RGB_mosaic_25cm_v4p2/{z}/{x}/{y}.png

(valid zoom levels are 11:19)

Unfortunately, there doesn't seem to be any easy way to simply add this to the providers brought in by `leaflet.providers`. What is the best way to "point" Leaflet at such a "custom" endpoint??

NOTE: I've made an attempt, by "forking" the `leaflet.providers` package and adding a "M20" provider using the above, but it only "sort-of" works. I can observe when forced invalid requests for tiles are made by Leaflet (ie "good errors"), but I'm not actually seeing tiles when valid requests are made (no errors are seen in e.g. Chrome console). I know that Leaflet is doing the slippy math correctly. 

Advice is welcome!!

title: Store the supported provider information in a static htmldependency; (Restores static Rmd/Qmd support)
description:
`{leaflet}` currently sets its `package.src` to `providers_loaded()$src` when `providers.src` is retrieved ([link](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/blob/1c06a658d7aba355f3f602ee52a8266a6a3a07a1/R/zzz.R#L15-L17)). 

It would be nice if the default providers being loaded came from a static htmldependency to avoid always using a temp file. This would require that `leaflet.providers` perform work similar to https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/blob/1c06a658d7aba355f3f602ee52a8266a6a3a07a1/R/plugin-providers.R#L92-L107. 

I don't know if this means we should add a `export_html_dep()` method (or something similar) so that others could save their non-standard `{leaflet.providers}` version just as we would do internally.

If resolved, it would fix https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/issues/732 and https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/issues/843 (or any leaflet output in an rmarkdown / quarto document).

title: Update to leaflet-providers@2.0.0
description:
As of 2023-08-25, leaflet-providers 2.0.0 isn't on npm yet. When it lands, we'll need to update our package and we should do so as early as possible.

> Ian from Stadia Maps here! I'm just making the rounds of libraries with decent traffic and came across this issue. Just a heads-up that the PR to address this in leaflet-providers upstream (https://github.com/leaflet-extras/leaflet-providers/pull/520) was opened a few weeks ago but just merged recently. I can't speak for the maintainers of that package, but it sounds like the 2.0.0 release will probably go out to npm later this week.
> 
> As with the similar OpenLayers PR, it's a breaking change (instead of provider names like `Stamen.Toner`, they will now be `Stadia.StamenToner`, since we're hosting the tiles but are still branded + contain attribution to Stamen), hence the major semver bump. I'm not sure what that means for your API, but just thought I'd drop in to flag that in case you need to do something similar. Feel free to tag me if you have any questions!

_Originally posted in https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet.providers/issues/25#issuecomment-1689997694_

title: Update leaflet-providers for continued access to Stamen map tiles
description:
Quoting from https://github.com/leaflet-extras/leaflet-providers/issues/519:

> Stamen will tiles will be migrated to Stadia on october 31 ref :
> 
> > Stadia Maps has [partnered with Stamen Design](http://maps.stamen.com/stadia-partnership/) to host their iconic map styles. If you are currently accessing Stamen map tiles via the Fastly CDN or a Stamen domain, you'll need to make a few (small!) changes to keep on using these maps after August 31, 2023. After this point, we will start progressive brownouts before the old URLs stop working entirely on October 31, 2023.
> 
> https://docs.stadiamaps.com/guides/migrating-from-stamen-map-tiles/
> https://stamen.com/here-comes-the-future-of-stamen-maps/

`leaflet-providers` has been updated to use the new Stadia URLs. For Stamen tiles to continue to work with `{leaflet}`, the new `leaflet-providers` is needed.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
Cc @schloerke

The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: entire_lizard*
